newsitem.title: GERMANY: German hostages not released in Yemen after all.
newsitem.headline: German hostages not released in Yemen after all.

text.p: Seven German hostages reported on Tuesday to have been released by kidnappers in Yemen have not been freed after all, Bonn's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday.
Spokesman Martin Erdmann said in response to an enquiry that the men had not arrived in the Yemeni capital Sanaa as expected, which meant that their release must have been delayed.

Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel instructed the German ambassador, Helga Strachwitz, to request an immediate meeting with Yemen's President Ali Abdullah Saleh to try to shed light on the hostages' situation.

The seven men, aged between 30 and 45, were kidnapped by local tribesmen last week while riding motorcycles through the Wadi al-Dabaat area between Mahra and Hadramaut, some 770 km (480 miles) to the east of Sanaa.
A Yemeni security official had said on Tuesday the kidnappers had agreed to release the Germans after security forces and troops tightened a siege on them.

He said last-minute negotiations had centred on the tribesmen's demand of a government amnesty in return for releasing their hostages. The official declined to say whether any of the demands had been met.
Kidnapping is a common ploy by tribesmen holding grievances against the government or foreign oil firms operating in Yemen, one of the Arab world's most impoverished countries.

Dozens of tourists, diplomats and other foreigners have been seized in recent years. The tribesmen have tried to use the foreigners, who have included a U.S. diplomat and a Saudi ambassador, as bargaining chips.
Siege by security forces has been the usual government response.
In the latest incident, the tribesmen wanted to pressure the government to bring to justice an alleged Yemeni swindler who sold them cars smuggled from Gulf Arab states.
